s: The unit concerns Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems and LightRAG, a framework designed to improve retrieval for large language models. s: This unit concerns Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems that integrate external knowledge sources with large language models to produce more accurate, relevant, domain-specific, and up-to-date responses. s: The unit compares RAG, LC, and SELF-ROUTE across Gemini-1.5-Pro, GPT-4O, and GPT-3.5-Turbo on LongBench datasets, finding that LC generally outperforms RAG while SELF-ROUTE approaches LC performance with fewer tokens. SELF-ROUTE routes queries to RAG when the retrieved context appears sufficient and sends other queries to LC, reducing token usage while preserving accuracy. The analysis examines retrieval failures, retriever variation, synthetic-data artifacts, and methods for limiting models’ use of internal knowledge. Results using the Dragon retriever and non-commonsense subsets broadly support the reported trends.

s: RAG generally underperforms LC, although it can outperform LC for GPT-3.5-Turbo on the longer ∞Bench En.QA and En.MC datasets when the context exceeds the model’s context window. Its failures are associated with multi-step reasoning, general or complex queries, and implicit questions requiring broad context understanding. RAG uses fewer input tokens than LC and can answer a substantial portion of queries, motivating its use within SELF-ROUTE.

l: LC, Retrieval Augmented Generation or Long-Context LLMs?, opening .. Exclusion of LLM’s internal knowledge
s: LC consistently outperforms RAG across the evaluated models on average, with especially large advantages for Gemini-1.5-Pro and GPT-4O. It provides the fallback prediction in SELF-ROUTE for queries that RAG cannot answer and generally achieves higher performance at greater token cost. Its performance is also used to assess the effect of prompting models to rely only on the provided passage.

l: SELF-ROUTE, Retrieval Augmented Generation or Long-Context LLMs?, opening .. Exclusion of LLM’s internal knowledge
s: SELF-ROUTE first asks the model to determine whether a query is answerable from retrieved chunks and accepts the RAG answer when it is, otherwise sending the query to LC with the full context. It substantially reduces token usage while achieving performance comparable to LC, surpassing RAG by more than 5% across the three models. Its routing behavior and performance vary by model and dataset, and its optimal retrieval value k depends on task characteristics and performance requirements.
